name: Tangzu Wan'er S.G II
notes: Single DD budget IEM (~$22). Bass-heavy tuning — the elevated low-end comes at the cost of mids clarity and treble detail for neutral-preferring listening. Instruments feel veiled behind the warm bass. Treble detail and air are lacking. Comfort is good. Value scored relative to preference fit, not raw price-to-performance.
summary:
Sound Signature: Neutral / Balanced
Even across all frequencies — versatile and accurate without strong colouration.

✅ Strong areas: Fit & Build.
✅ Smooth, non-fatiguing treble — sibilance is well-controlled.
ℹ️ Punchy but muddy bass — good impact, but fast bass passages may sound bloated.
🎵 Best for: General listening.

Verdict: Decent (5.6/10) — Gets the job done, some compromises.

name: CrinEar Daybreak
notes: Crinacle's first mass-produced tribrid (1DD+2BA+2mPT). Tuned to IEF 2025 Curve — reference-grade neutral. Micro-planar tweeters give excellent treble extension and air. Clean, controlled bass with natural mids. Ergonomic filled-resin shell with modular 3.5mm/4.4mm cable.
summary:
Sound Signature: Neutral / Balanced
Even across all frequencies — versatile and accurate without strong colouration.

✅ Strong areas: Bass, Mids, Treble, Fit & Build.
🎵 Best for: EDM, Hip-hop, Live rock, Vocals, Acoustic.

Verdict: Very Good (7/10) — Solid performer with minor flaws.
